texts.facts: 1. The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) for compensation relates to grievous injury suffered by the claimant Kunal in a road accident that took place on 01.04.2018 at about 07:50 PM, Near Gate No. 2, Nagal Dewat Gaon, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi, regarding which one FIR No.143/18 was registered at PS Vasant Kunj South. 2. The offending vehicle involved in this case is a three wheeler bearing registration No. DL-1LL-1986, which at the relevant time of accident was being driven by respondent no.1 Vipin Kumar, registered in the name of respondent no. 2 Jitender Kumar, subsequently purchased by respondent no. 3 Vijay and thereafter, purchased by respondent no. 4 Dharmender. Case of the claimant 3. It is the case of the claimant that on 01.04.2018, he along with his mother Smt. Poonam and sister Parul were going on scooty No. DL-3SCD-7119 from Nangal Devat Redlight to his residence at Vasant Kunj Enclave, Delhi which was being driven by his mother Smt. Poonam. When they reached at Gate No. 2, Nangal Devat Village, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. DL-1LL-1986, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner, came from Vasant Kunj Enclave side in a wrong direction and hit their scooty from the front due to which they fell down on the road and sustained injuries. It is further stated that the claimant was taken to Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi where his MLC was prepared by the doctors. Case of respondent no. 2 4. Respondent no. 2/owner filed his reply to the DAR wherein it is stated that he has sold the alleged offending vehicle to respondent no. 3 Vijay on 23.09.2023 against a total sale consideration of Rs.59,000/- and the said fact was reduced in writing between them in the presence of witnesses. It is further stated that Sh. Vijay had also put his signatures on delivery receipt and he had also given Form 35 duly signed by him to Sh. Vijay for the purpose of transfer of the aforesaid vehicle. It is further stated that the the accident took place on account of negligent driving of Poonam who was driving her scooty without having valid driving license. It is further stated that Poonam was driving her scooty with two pillion riders which is clear violation of traffic rules and norms. Case of respondent no. 4 5. Respondent no. 4 filed his reply to the DAR wherein it is stated that he is not entitled to pay any compensation to the claimant as he has no concern with the alleged accident. It is further stated that the rider of scooty was driving her scooty with pillion riders and was not holding any valid and effective driving license at the time of accident. It is further stated that the accident took place due to sole and absolute negligence on the part of rider of the scooty. 6. Vide order dated 14.11.2022, respondents no. 1 and 2 were proceeded against ex-parte. 7. It is pertinent to mention that vide order dated 08.03.2019, three connected DARs bearing DAR Nos. 635/18, 636/18 & 641/18 arising out of the same accident were consolidated for the purpose of Kunal vs Vipin Kumar (Without Insurance And Dl) on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29679609/ 2 trial and DAR No. 635/18 was directed to be treated as the lead case for recording of evidence. Issues 8. On 08.03.2019, the following consolidated issues were framed by this Tribunal :- 1. Whether Kunal (minor injured in D-635/18), Smt. Poonam (injured in D-636/18) and Parul (minor injured in D-641/18) sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 02.04.2018 at about 07:50 PM, Road Near Gate No. 2, Nagal Dewat Gaon, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. DL-1LL-1986 being driven by respondent no. 1, registered in the name of respondent no. 2, alleged to have been sold by respondent no. 2 to respondent no. 3 and then respondent no. 3 to respondent no. 4 ? OPP. 3. Relief. Claimant's evidence 9. In support of claim, Smt. Poonam, mother of the claimant examined herself as PW1, who is also an injured in the connected matter. She tendered her evidence by way of affidavit as Ex. PW1/A and relied upon the following documents :- (i). Ex. PW1/1 is the copy of Aadhaar card of her son. (ii). Ex. PW1/2 is the MLC of his son. (iii). Ex.PW1/3 (colly) are the treatment record of his son. (iv). Ex. PW1/4 (colly) are the medical bills of his son. (v). Ex. PW1/5 (colly) is the DAR filed by the IO. Ex. PW1/11 (colly) are her medical bills. 10. The claimant also examined Ms. Parul, sister of the claimant, who is also an injured in the connected matter, as PW2. (iv). Ex. PW2/4 (colly) are her treatment record. (v). Ex. PW2/5 (colly) are her medical bills. (vi). Ex. PW1/5 is the DAR filed by the IO. Ex. PW2/6 (colly) are the photographs showing her injuries. (viii). Mark A (colly) are the copies of educational qualification documents. 11. The claimant also examined Sh. Amandeep Singh, Senior Billing Executive from Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi as PW4 who has placed on record his authority letter as Ex. PW4/1, final bills with details of claimant as Ex. PW4/2 (colly) to Ex. PW4/9 (colly) and discharge summaries of claimant as Ex. PW4/10 (colly). 12. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.R2W1/A and relied upon copies of sale letter, delivery receipts and NOC as Mark R2W1/1 (colly). He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. DW3/1A and relied upon the copy of his Aadhaar card as Ex.DW3/1 (OSR) and the policy of insurance as Ex. DW3/2 (OSR). Kunal vs Vipin Kumar (Without Insurance And Dl) on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29679609/ 4 33 . The claimant examined Sh. Amandeep Singh, Senior Billing Executive from Indian Spinal Injuries Centre, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi as PW4 who has proved the final bills with details of claimant as Ex. PW4/2 (colly) to Ex. PW4/9 (colly) and discharge summaries of claimant as Ex. PW4/10 (colly). 34. PW1 has tendered on record medical bills of her son as Ex. PW1/4 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 2,05,185/-.
texts.arguments: He argued that Smt. Poonam was not holding a valid driving license and was riding the two wheeler with two pillion riders. He also argued that the three wheeler was not coming from the wrong side. He submitted that on the road where the accident took place, there was two-way traffic and it was not one-way traffic road. 21. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Saraswati Palariya and Ors. Vs New India Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors., 2019 ACJ 42 has held that driving without a driving license may expose the person to other liabilities but no inference of contributory negligence can be drawn on that basis. 22. In Mohammed Siddique & Anr. Vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. AIR 2020 SUPREME COURT 520, it has been held as follows: Kunal vs Vipin Kumar (Without Insurance And Dl) on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29679609/ 5 "13. The fact that the deceased was riding on a motor cycle along with the driver and another, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence. Section 194 C inserted by the Amendment Act 32 of 2019, prescribes a penalty for violation of safety measures for motor cycle drivers and pillion riders. Therefore, an adverse inference is drawn against the respondent no.1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310. 25. Reliance is being placed upon the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Meera Devi & ors., 2021 LawSuit (Del) 2021 wherein it was held that "......in view of Delhi Motor Accident Claim Tribunal Rules, 2008, contents of DAR has to be presumed to be correct and read in evidence without formal proof of the same unless proof to the contrary was produced." 26. Chargesheet was also filed against the respondent no.1/driver of the vehicle. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently. It has been further observed that even when the accused was acquitted in the criminal case, the same will have no effect on the assessment of liability required in respect of motor accident cases by the Tribunal. Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability. 28. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:- Pecuniary damages (Special Damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising : (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages) 39. In the Judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Rakesh Sharma @ Rakesh & Anr. Vs. Ashok & Ors., MAC APP No. 282/2022, decided on 04.03.2025, the following was held :- "19. Subsequently, in Master Ayush vs. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., (2022) 7 SCC 738, the Apex Court while considering the grant of compensation to the parents on account of injuries suffered by a five-year-old child, relied upon Kajal (Supra) and observed that the notional income should be calculated on the basis of minimum wages payable to a skilled worker." 40. The liability to pay compensation is of the registered owner and in this context, reliance is placed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar & Ors., 2018 AIR (SC) 983, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with a case of multiple transfers of an uninsured vehicle has allowed an appeal filed by a purchaser of the offending vehicle and has [LEAKAGE_MASK] the judgment of the Hon'ble Punjab & Haryana High Court holding him liable to pay compensation, which in turn set-aside the judgment/award passed by a Claims Tribunal holding the registered owner of offending vehicle, along with driver thereof, to be liable for making payment of an award passed in the said case. The following was held in this case :- Kunal vs Vipin Kumar (Without Insurance And Dl) on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29679609/ 13 "12. In Dr T V Jose, this Court observed that there can be transfer of title by payment of consideration and delivery of the car. The mandate of the law must be fulfilled. In the circumstances of the case, there shall be no order as to costs." 63. The above propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Naveen Kumar (supra) have even been followed and reiterated subsequently by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Prakash Chand Daga Vs. Saveta Sharma & Ors., 2018 LawSuit (SC) 176, wherein the findings of the Hon'ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana holding a registered owner to be liable in place of purchaser and possessor thereof, was upheld. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held the following :- "9. The law is thus well settled and can be summarised:- Kunal vs Vipin Kumar (Without Insurance And Dl) on 20 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29679609/ 14 Even though in law there would be a transfer of ownership of the vehicle, that, by itself, would not absolve the party, in whose name the vehicle stands in RTO records, from liability to a third person. Merely because the vehicle was transferred does not mean that such registered owner stands absolved of his liability to a third person. The High Court was therefore absolutely right in allowing the appeal.
